query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: pedagogy_adaptation_quality
per_column.rationale: A genuine driver axis for satisfaction; categorises how teaching was adapted. Samples map well (ED-0002 innovative kitchen-chemistry, ED-0003 absent). ED-0005 'passive_or_unchanged' is a defensible reading though the text is more about student non-participation than teacher pedagogy, a mild stretch.

per_column.name: peer_social_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Distinct social-dimension driver relevant to satisfaction. ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' and ED-0004 'not_present' are well grounded. ED-0001 'significant_loss_of_community' is inferred from 'miss raising my hand' — reasonable but somewhat generous.

per_column.name: teacher_feedback_and_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Useful responsiveness axis. ED-0004 'timely_and_detailed' and ED-0003 'slow_or_minimal' are supported. ED-0005 'slow_or_minimal' is weak — the text describes participation issues, not teacher feedback speed, a minor overreach.

per_column.name: async_format_benefit
per_column.rationale: Captures a specific benefit (self-paced/recorded) distinguishing high satisfaction. ED-0004 'strong_benefit' from 'pause and take notes' is well grounded; 'not_present' for silent rows is correct behaviour. Skewed distribution reduces leverage slightly but still discriminating.

per_column.name: student_engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Engagement is a core plausible driver of satisfaction. Samples align well (ED-0002 actively engaged, ED-0005 disengaged). Slight risk of proxying satisfaction itself but distinct enough to model on.

per_column.name: subject_remote_format_fit
per_column.rationale: Good axis to group by subject/remote suitability. ED-0001 algebra low_fit and ED-0004 history high_fit are reasonable. Some values may partly track overall sentiment rather than subject-specific fit, a mild grounding concern.

judge.rationale: All six columns supply genuine, distinct analytical axes (pedagogy, peer loss, feedback, async benefit, engagement, subject fit) directly relevant to explaining low learning satisfaction and its drivers; none are near-constant or trivial restatements. Values are generally sound readings of the source text, with a few generous inferences (e.g., ED-0005 feedback/pedagogy labels, ED-0001 community loss) but no invented facts or contradictions, and 'not_present' is used appropriately for silent rows.
